text: So you're the one who put Harl on his back on the quay. The whole yard heard. Stand up straight. Hm. Arms like a deckhand, eyes like you've lost your own name.
Ambrose saw smugglers off the south cove? Then he's right, and they're Grell's. Fists won't shift a camp of them. Steel will.
That rack. Every kind of weapon a sailor's ever swung, and a few they shouldn't. Take one down, try it on the dummies, put it back, take the next. Keep the one your hands like.
Only one. The rest Haldor sells, and he'll want paying. Choose well.

story_rack.text: The rack, by the north fence. Try them on the dummies. When one feels like yours, keep it.

story_drills.text: The dummies won't hit themselves. Every move on the list, then we talk smugglers.

story_shrine.text: Up the long stair, past the gate. Master Isao. Answer him honestly and quickly, and don't touch the bell.

story_smugglers.text: The smugglers are still on the south beach, past the cove. They won't clear out on their own. Off you go.

text: Back already, and bleeding about the right amount. The smugglers are done? Good.

Listen. Every fight you live through teaches you something, whether you like it or not. Enough of it and you grow. And every weapon you swing learns you back: use it and it opens up, new cuts, new tricks.
Open your skill map with K and see what your hand's learned. Here, a head start: one of my drills. Again. Again. There. Feel that?
Something else woke in you down there. I saw it in the last swing: a current, under the strength. Sailors call it Edy.
I can't teach that. Master Isao can. Up the long stair, at the shrine on the terrace. He'll read what kind you have and show you what it's for.
After that, Grell. His crew holds the old harbour on the north-west beach. A real pirate captain, not some smuggler. He's been bleeding this town for years.

story_grell.text: Grell's at the old harbour on the north-west beach. He won't come to you, and he won't go easy. Get some fights under your belt first.

text: You. Captain {captain}. You walk like someone who's never been hit properly.
Retired Admiralty man, twenty years. These dummies are my pupils now. They listen better than recruits ever did.
Left click. Three cuts in a chain, the third one hits hardest. Click again just as a swing ends to keep the chain going.
Go on, hit a dummy. They don't hit back. Yet.
Right click. You wind up, lunge forward, then you're open for a moment. Commit or don't bother.
A heavy blow ends fights. A missed one ends you.
Left Ctrl rolls you in the direction you're moving. While you're rolling, nothing touches you.
Roll through an attack, not away from it. Cowards roll away.
Q. Hold your blade up at the instant a blow lands and you'll turn it aside. Too early or too late and you eat it.
High risk. The best kind.
Mail, plate, a helm that's turned a cutlass or two. I'll take armour you've outgrown. Not cheap. Neither is a funeral.
Blades you'll want from Haldor, at the forge west of the plaza. Tell him Vey sent you. He'll charge you more.
Saw things on the Grand Patrol that weren't in any manual. Stones that hummed. Water that ran uphill.
Command said forget it. I said no. So here I am, teaching straw men to fear me.

bye.text: Keep your guard up and your blade wet.
